top_choice_rationale: The GLP-1 prize to Drucker, Holst and Mojsov rewards a specific discovery chain (incretin physiology and proglucagon processing, the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide) that changed its field, with effects on glycaemia, weight and cardiovascular and renal outcomes confirmed independently in large trials, so maturity is not in doubt. The main risks are Mojsov's contested priority against Habener and the exclusion of Knudsen; the citation scope on physiology and the active form keeps the award on discovery. These risks do not outweigh the achievement, so awarding is preferable to no award.
